## Selecting text in programs that use the mouse

- Claude Code, Codex and other full-screen programs that use the mouse no longer take every click and drag. By default they get only the scroll wheel, so dragging selects text, copy-on-select works and right-click pastes without holding Shift.
- A new Mouse in programs setting chooses what such programs get: scrolling only (the new default), clicks and scrolling (the old behaviour), or never. Each session can override it. Shift swaps the two, so a click to the program is still Shift+click away.

## Agent tabs

- Persistent tabs now show the title an agent sets itself, so a Claude Code tab reads as the conversation topic instead of "claude". The status glyph agents put in front of their titles is left out, so the tab doesn't flicker with the spinner.

## Terminal

- Legacy computing symbols (wedges, triangles, eighth blocks, diagonals, circles) and octants are drawn by Resesh itself, like box drawing, instead of showing as empty boxes when the font lacks them.
- Programs that ask for the terminal size, or ask to be told when it changes, now get an answer.
- Programs that send large synchronized frames back to back, such as notcurses-demo, no longer freeze the screen on an old frame.
- Terminals come back if recovering from a lost graphics device fails part way, instead of staying blank.
- Dictation and the emoji panel work while a key is held.
- Telnet BBS menus no longer freeze when "report 80x25" is on and the screen ends on a cursor move, and typed text keeps one encoding.

## Fixes

This release also fixes a long list of races, mostly around things that end while something else is still going on:

- Closing a tab mid-connect no longer leaks the connection, and closing a file pane stops a hung SFTP connect.
- Login prompts from closed tabs no longer appear later, and closing a tab works even if it changes, or moves to another window, while its close dialog is open.
- Input is no longer sent before a reconnect has succeeded.
- Each SSHFS mount gets its own drive letter, even when two tabs mount at once, and closing the tab stops a mount that is still coming up.
- Stopping a tunnel while it starts no longer leaves its listener open.
- Recordings stop cleanly when the disk fills, and say so in the terminal.
- Settings files that could not be read are never saved over.
- Only one backup or import wizard, and one import review from Welcome, opens at a time.
- Command history keeps the selected command when the filter changes, and command marks stay with the right command after a reconnect.
- Focus returns to the right place when the palette and history overlay replace each other.

Choose the x64 download for Intel or AMD PCs. Choose ARM64 only for Windows on ARM devices.
